- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a recent spike in sentiment, apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out overshoot.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast toward mean reversion trend.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should not overfit to recent extremes — use 3–5 day smoothing filter.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and forecast diverges >5% from 18-day history, revert to historical mean or 15-day SMA.
